PREFACE 
 I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home 
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby present 
this One Hundred Eighty Fourth Report on Action Taken by Government on the 
recommendations/observations contained in the 179 th Report (ATR on 137 th Report) of the Committee 
on the Rehabilitation of J&K Migrants. 
 
2. The One Hundred and Seventy Ninth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on 19 th 
February, 2014.  After presentation of the Report, the copies thereof were sent to the Ministry of Home 
Affairs requesting them to furnish Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee 
contained in the Report.  
 
3. The Ministry furnished the Action Taken Notes on the 179 th Report on the Action Taken on the 
Recommendations in Committee's 137 th Report on the Rehabilitation of J&K Migrants to the 
Committee on 1st September, 2014.  The Minister of Home Affairs laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha 
the status of implementation of recommendations contained in the said report of the Committee, on  
16th December, 2014 pursuant to the direction of the Chairman, Rajya Sabha and presented the same in 
the Rajya Sabha on 17th December, 2014.   
 
4.
 The Committee, thereafter, considered the draft 184 th Action Taken Report on the 
recommendations/observations contained in the 179 th Report (ATR on 137 th Report) of the Committee 
on the Rehabilitation of J&K Migrants and adopted the same in its meeting held on 22nd January, 2015.

REPORT 
 The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of 
Home Affairs on the recommendations on Rehabilitation of J&K Migrants, contained in the One 
Hundred and Seventy Ninth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Home Affairs on the Action Taken on the Recommendations in Committee’s 137 th Report on the 
above subject.  The Report was presented in Parliament 19thFebruary 2014. 
 
2. Action Taken Notes (ATNs) received from the Ministry of  Home Affairs in respect of the 
observations/recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Seventy Ninth Report have been 
categorized as follows: 
 
Chapter I: The observations/recommendations, which have been accepted by the Gov ernment:  
Paras: 2.1.18, 2.1.22, 2.1.26, 2.1.34, 2.1.38, 2.1.46, 2.1.76, 2.1.104, 2.1.106, 2.1.125, 2.1.137, 2.1.138, 
2.1.141, 2.1.145 (of the  One Hundred and Seventy Ninth  Report) Total recommendations-14;   
 
 The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted fourteen of its 
recommendations as mentioned in Chapter – I of the Report. 
Chapter II: The observations/recommendations which the Committee does not desire to pursue 
in view o f the Government’s replies: - Paras: 2.1.9, 2.1.16, 2.1.20, 2.1.84, 2.1.90, 2.1.92, 2.1.94, 
(ibid) Total recommendations-7;   
 
 The Committee is convinced with the explanation furnished by the Ministry and, therefore, 
does not want to pursue the recommendations further. 
Chapter III: The observations/recommendations in respect of which the Committee is not 
satisfied with the replies of the Ministry: Paras:  2.1.11, 2.1.24, 2.1.30, 2.1.32, 2.1.60, 2.1.98, 
2.1.124, 2.1.143, 2.1.147 (ibid) Total recommendations-9. 
  
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of nine of its 
recommendations contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should take further necessary 
action and furnish convincing replies in respect of those recommendations within a time frame of three  
months after presentation of the Report. 
 
Chapter-IV: The observations/recommendations in respect of which final replies of  the 
Government have not been received:  Para:  2.1.13, 2.1.28, 2.1.43, 2.1.44, 2.1.47, 2.1.51, 2.1.53, 
2.1.62, 2.1.67, 2.1.72, 2.1.74, 2.1.82, 2.1.87, 2.1.96, 2.1.102, 2.1.109, 2.1.110, 2.1.111, 2.1.112, 
2.1.115, 2.1.117, 2.1.120, 2.1.122, 2.1.129, 2.1.133, 2.1.149(ibid) Total recommendations-26. 
  
In respect of the twenty five recommendations placed in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has either 
furnished interim replies or couched its response in vague terms. In this Chapter, several 
recommendations pertain to implementation of PM’s Package.  The Government in its action taken on 
the recommendations on the implementation of the PM’s package has stated that the State government 
has sent the package to the Union Government to revise it.  The Committee expresses its concern  that 
even before full implementation, the Package has been sent for revision and that too after many years 
of announcement of the Package.  The Committee hopes that at least now the package would be 
revised without delay and implemented soon.   
 
3. The Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken 
Notes in respect of the recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the 
intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee within three months. 
 
4. The para-wise details of the ATNs are being discussed, as per the categorisation indicated 
above, in the succeeding Chapters. 
 
 

CHAPTER-I 
 
OBSERVATIONS /RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH  
HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT 
 
1.1 CONDUCIVE ENVIRONMENT FOR RETURN TO THE VALLEY 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.1.1 The Committee advises the Government to be extremely cautious in clearing the names of 
militants for surrender. Militants who have shown signs of change of heart may only be 
accommodated.  
(Para 2.1.18 of the 179th Report) 
Action Taken  
 
1.1.2 Surrender policies of Government of J&K stipulate th at “the authority accepting the surrender 
shall have reason to believe that the terrorist concerned has undergone Change of heart and wants to 
renounce violence”. The Government clears the names of militants for surrender after taking due care 
in this respect.  
 
1.1.3 However, the State Government has again been advised vide MHA letter dated 25-06-2014 to 
take necessary actions in accordance to the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
1.2 CONDITION OF PANDITS LIVING IN THE VALLEY  
 
Recommendation  
 
1.2.1 The Committee notes that more than 600 families are still residing in the Valley. The 
Committee also notes that about 31 families had to be shifted to a transit camp due to security reasons. 
The Committee in view of the prevailing conditions desires that the courage of such Kashmiri Pandit 
families still residing in the Valley should be appreciated and they should be provided appropriate 
security. They may also be provided other facilities as may be required. 
(Para 2.1.22 ibid) 
 
Action Taken  
 
1.2.2 As reported by the State Government, action has already been taken on the matter and 31 
families who were living in a transit camp in the Valley due to security reasons have been all otted flats 
in the Valley, which are constructed under PM’s Package -2008. The State Government is also taking 
all necessary steps to ensure security and other facilities to the Kashmiri Pandit families living  in the 
Valley. 
 
1.3 THE ROLE OF MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.3.1 The Committee is of the view that the situation of Migrants still remains neglected several 
years after the exodus started. It may be due to extreme difficulty in resettlement or wrong policies, but 
whatever may be the case the situation on the ground remains grim. The Ministry of Home Affairs 
being the nodal agency cannot shirk away its responsibility for not being able to improve the situation 
on the ground. The Committee exhorts the Ministry to look for different solutions if the previous 
policies have not worked. 
(Para 2.1.26 ibid) 

Action Taken  
 
1.3.2 The Ministry of Home Affairs has taken a number of relief and rehabilitation measures for the 
Kashmiri migrants, such as, grant of monthly cash assistance to eligible families, education fac ilities, 
allotment of 237 DDA flats to migrants in Delhi, construction and allotment of 5242 two roomed 
tenements at Jammu to migrants staying in camps, construction of 200 flats at Badgam, PM’s Package 
for return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants, etc.  MHA would continue to take measures for the 
welfare/ rehabilitation of the Kashmiri migrants. The suggestion of the Committee has been noted and 
would be kept in view in framing packages/schemes regarding rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants in 
future. 
 
 
1.4 WHITE PAPER ON EXODUS OF MIGRANTS 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.4.1 There is a demand from some migrant associations for establishment of provincial authority in 
the valley for issue of State Subject Certificates and other relevant certificates to local migrants. The 
Committee feels that keeping in mind the practical difficulties being faced by the Migrants, the demand 
may be looked into. 
(Para 2.1.34 ibid) 
Action Taken  
 
1.4.2 As informed by the State Government, for issuing State Subject Certificates and other relevant 
certificates to local migrants, State Authorities are available in each district in the Valley. 
 
 
1.5 REASONS FOR FAILURE OF SCHEMES 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.5.1 The Committee strongly recommends that interaction with the representatives of the Migrant 
groups should be frequently conducted in order to get the relevant feedback. In the light of dismal 
response to the schemes, such feedback would be of immense importance for focused implementation 
and course correction of the policy. 
(Para 2.1.38 ibid) 
Action Taken  
 
1.5.2 As informed by the State Government a Sub Committee has already been formed consisting of 
the non official members of the Apex Advisory Committee in order to get the feedback for focused 
implementation and course correction of the policy/scheme for rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants. 
 
1.6 EMPLOYMEN T UNDER PM’S PACKAGE 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.6.1 The Committee is of the opinion that the State Government's approach should be flexible 
enough to consider transfer requests on compassionate grounds from any part of the State to any other 
part of the State especially in the case of female employees. As far as possible, female employees 
should be posted in areas close to the areas of their husbands' posting. The Committee is further of the 
opinion that the 21 requests of inter-district transfers of female employ ees, close to their husbands’ 
workplace may be considered positively on priority basis. 
(Para 2.1.46 ibid) 

 
Action taken  
 
1.6.2 The J&K State Government has informed that 21 requests of inter district transfer of female 
employees has already been disposed off and action is being taken on such new requests on pr iority 
basis. 
 
 
1.7 FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE FOR UNEMPLOYED YOUTHS 
 
Recommendation  
  
1.7.1 The Committee recommends that the State Government should formulate a policy instead of 
considering their cases on case to case basis, to assist the militancy affected entrepreneurs to revive 
industrial activity among the affected community. 
(Para 2.1.76 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
1.7.2 As informed by the State Government, the number of such entrepreneurs is not large so the 
cases are being dealt on case to case basis. 
 
 
1.8 PROBLEMS AND DELAY IN VERIFICATIONS 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.81 The Committee recommends that all issues related to the verification process may be resolved 
at the earliest so that request for cash relief made by genuine claimants (in Delhi) may be addressed. 
(Para 2.1.104 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
1.8.2 As informed by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi that instruction has been issued for resolving all 
issues related to the verification process of Kashmiri Migrants and to ensure release of AMR to the 
eligible migrants in time. 
 
1.9 HOUSING ASSISTANCE 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.9.1 The Committee recommends that the verification process for allotment of remaining dwelling 
units may be conducted soon so that they can be allotted soon as there has already been considerable 
delay in allotment. 
(Para 2.1.106 ibid) 
Action taken  
1.9.2 As informed by the J&K State Government, all the dwelling units i.e. 5242 two room 
tenements have been allotted to the deserving migrant families. 
 
1.10 PROBLEMS OF JAGTI 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.10.1 The Committee recommends that allotment of the remaining flats in Jagti may be done on 
priority basis and the verification process for the same may be completed as soon as possible. 

 (Para 2.1.125 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
1.10.2 As informed by the State Government, the process of allotment of flats in Jagti has been 
completed. 
 
1.11 UPDATION OF VOTERS LIST OF THE MIGRANTS AND ISSUE OF PHOTO I-
CARDS 
 
Recommendation  
  
1.11.1 The Committee recommends that the issues of updation of voter lists and simplification of 
voting procedures for the Migrants may be appropriately taken up with the Election Commission so 
that the Migrants are not made bereft of their voting rights as citizens of the State. 
(Para 2.1.137 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
1.11.2 Updation of electoral rolls is being done regularly, in which migrant families too are given an 
option to incorporate/delete any member of their family. On the basis of inputs provided by the 
individual migrant family in the prescribed form, the updation of electoral rolls is made accordingly. 
Updation of electoral rolls, as per the notification of the Election Commission of India, in respect of 
Kashmiri migrants too is taking place regularly for enabling them to exercise their voting rights. 
 
1.12 UPDATION OF VOTERS LIST OF THE MIGRANTS AND ISSUE OF PHOTO I-
CARDS 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.12.1 The Committee is surprised by the cumbersome nature of the electoral process designed for the 
Migrants. No wonder that they allege the whole system has been instituted to discourage them. While 
that may not be the case, simplification of the process is obviously required. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Government may take up the matter with Election Commission so that the 
Migrants can rightfully take part in the electoral process like rest of their fellow citizens. 
 (Para 2.1.138 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
1.12.2 In order to facilitate the migrants of the Valley to participate in the electoral process, a special 
arrangement is being made by Election Commission of India during Elections by establishing special 
polling booths at Jammu, Udhampur and Delhi for the Constituencies of the Valley. 
 
1.13 UPDATION OF VOTERS LIST OF THE MIGRANTS AND ISSUE OF PHOTO I-
CARDS 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.13.1 The Committee during its deliberations with the Migrants was informed by several 
representatives that they face tremendous difficulties in getting various certificates for establishing 
identity, residency etc. The Committee is of the opinion that since the representatives have complained 
about the cumbersomeness of the process, the same may be simplified and made Migrant friendly. The 
entire procedure may be re-looked. 
(Para 2.1.141 ibid) 
Action taken  

1.13.2 As informed by the State Government, the migrant families are provided migrant ration cards 
depicting their original residential address in valley, present residential address, details of their 
dependents, etc.  The State Government has stated that they are following very simple procedure for 
obtaining certificates like PRC, Migration certificates, Age Relaxation Certificates etc. 
 
1.13.3 However, MHA has again advised the State Government vide letter dated 25-08-2014 to take 
necessary actions so that migrants can get their requisite certificates in time. 
 
1.14 APPOINTMENT ON COMPASSIONATE GROUND 
 
Recommendation  
 
1.14.1 The Committee is not satisfied with the routine reply given on a significant issue of giving 
employment to a family member of a Government employees/ civilian / member of an armed Forces or 
para military forces, who dies as a result of militancy related action or due to enemy action on the 
Line of Actual Control/International Border within the State of Jammu and Kashmir. The Committee 
strongly feels that such cases deserve due attention and disposal on priority. The Committee, therefore, 
strongly recommends that all cases of appointment on compassionate grounds should be decided at the 
earliest in a time bound manner, with proper monitoring at higher level. 
(Para 2.1.145 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
1.14.2 As informed by the State Government, they already have a policy for providing ex-gratia re lief 
and employment on compassionate grounds to Next of Kins (NOKs) of the victims of the militancy 
and the implementation of the policy is being monitored by the State Government. 
  
1.14.3 However, the State Government has again been advised vide MHA letter dated 25-06-2014 to 
take necessary actions in accordance to the recommendations of the Committee. 
 

 
CHAPTER-II 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE 
TO PURSUEIN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT'S REPLIES 
 
 
2.1 DECLARATION OF KASHMIRI MIGRANTS AS INTERNALLY DISPLACED 
PERSONS  
 
Recommendation  
 
2.1.1 The Committee desires that the Ministry should ensure that Migrants be provided all the 
facilities for rehabilitation as are provided to a displaced community. 
(Para 2.1.9 of the 179th Report) 
Action Taken  
 
2.1.2 The PM’s Package announced by the Prime Minister in 2008 for relief and rehabilitation of 
Kashmiri migrants provides for financial assistance for purchase/ construction/ repair of houses in the 
Valley, construction of transit accommodations, scholarship to the students, employment (Govt./ self-
employment), assistance for agriculture and horticulture and waiver of interest on unpaid loan etc. 
Besides, the eligible migrants are also getting monthly cash assistance and dry ration.  The fac ilities 
being provided are not considered in any way less than the facilities given to the displaced community. 
 
2.2. CONDUCIVE ENVIRONMENT FOR RETURN TO THE VALLEY 
 
Recommendation  
 
2.2.1 The Committee is saddened by the plight of Migrant families of Budgam who have been forced 
by the circumstances beyond their control to live in resettlement camp in their home State. The 
Committee, therefore, feels that the least the government can do is to provide them enough housing 
units for settlement. The Committee therefore impresses upon the Government that 505 units of transit 
accommodations may be allotted to them on priority basis. 
 (Para 2.1.16 ibid) 
Action Taken  
 
2.2.2 469 transit accommodations have been constructed in the Kashmir Valley under PM’s Package-
2008. As reported by the State Government, action has already been taken on the matter. 469 flats 
constructed under the PM’s Package -2008 have already been allotted to the migrants families 
including 31 locally migrant families within the Valley, who were living in a camp in the Valley due to 
security reasons. 
 
 
2.3 CONDUCIVE ENVIRONMENT FOR RETURN TO THE VALLEY 
 
Recommendation  
 
2.3.1 The Committee is of the opinion that strict action should be taken against perpetrators. The 
Government should also send a message to the affected persons with assurance that if their cases had 
not been filed, they should come forward to lodge their cases without any fear. The Committee would 
also like to be apprised of the status of filed cases along with conviction of perpetrators. 
 (Para 2.1.20 ibid) 
Action Taken  
 

2.3.2 The matter of maintenance of law & order falls under the purview of the State Government.  
The State Government of J&K has been requested by MHA vide letter dated 25-06-2014 to take 
necessary actions in accordance with the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
2.4 ISSUES RELATED TO TEACHERS  
 
Recommendation  
 
2.4.1 The Committee recommends that the cases of 221 teachers who have been deprived of 
employment due to overage may be sympathetically looked into as the people from the Migrant 
community are suffering from various handicaps and therefore deserve sympathy for the same. 
(Para 2.1.84 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
2.4.2 As informed by the State Government, the matter of 221 teachers would be dealt with as per 
guidelines and norms. Presently the matter is sub-judice. 
 
2.5 RELIEF TO MIGRANTS AT PAR WITH J&K RATES 
 
Recommendation  
 
2.5.1 The Committee recommends that all States should provide relief to J&K Migrants at par with 
J&K State so that they do not feel disadvantaged or discriminated. 
(Para 2.1.90 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
2.5.2 Based on the recommendation of the Committee, a fresh advisory has been issued by MHA in 
May 2014 to all the State/ UTs, where Kashmiri migrants are staying, for providing relief to the J&K 
migrants as par with J&K Government. 
 
2.6 RELIEF TO MIGRANTS AT PAR WITH J&K RATES 
 
Recommendation  
 
2.6.1 The Committee desires that action in regard to rehabilitation of displaced shopkeepers from 
the migrant community in INA market, New Delhi may be taken on priority basis. People from the 
migrant community who have left their native places due to conditions beyond their control should not 
face undue delays in the allotment of Stalls. 
(Para 2.1.92 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
2.6.2 Govt. of NCT of Delhi has informed that they have already approved allotment of tehbazari site 
of size measuring 7’x8’ to Kashmiri Migrants at ChanduLalBalmiki Marg, INA. A draw of lot in this 
respect held on 06-02-2012.  They have further informed that Flyover Project Division, PWD has 
made a request for shifting of these stalls to NDMC workshop area for the purpose of construction of 
elevated road over Bara PullaNallah Phase-II near INA Market.  South Delhi Municipal Corporation 
(SDMC) has expressed its no objection if the PWD Authorities shifts the said stalls with the 
consultation of land owning agency and the consent of the Kashmiri Migrants. The Govt. of NCT of 
Delhi has assured that they would vigorously follow up the matter for actions required to be taken in 
this regard. 
 
2.7 RELIEF TO MIGRANTS AT PAR WITH J&K RATES 
 

Recommendation  
 
2.7.1 The Committee is of the opinion that the pretext given that Kashmiri Migrants are not Indians 
for not allocating shops in INA market is highly objectionable. The complaint may be looked into and 
action may be initiated against people involved in such blatant discrimination. 
(Para 2.1.94 ibid) 
Action taken  
 
2.7.2 The Govt. of NCT of Delhi has informed that the Kashmiri Migrants have already been allotted 
36 shops measuring 7’x8’ at tehbazari site, ChanduLalBalmiki Marg, INA. 
 
 
 

CHAPTER-III 
OBSERVATIONS /RECOMMENDATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE 
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
 
3.1 CONDUCIVE ENVIRONMENT FOR RETURN TO THE VALLEY 
 
Recommendation  
 
3.1.1 The Committee is of the view that after so many years since the exodus took place and 
especially after declaration of ambitious packages for the return of Migrants, improvement on the 
ground has been scanty and just one family has returned to the Valley since the announcement of the 
package. There can be two explanations for such an extremely poor response from the community: 
either i) the package is not attractive enough; or ii) the environment is not safe for them to return. The 
Committee also notes that other components of the PM's Package except the employment and transit 
accommodation component could not be initiated as they can come into force only after the Migrant 
families return to the Valley. This has resulted in a strange situation where the families refuse to return 
as the environment is not conducive enough while the government refuses to pass the benefits to them 
as return is a precondition for availing the benefits. The Committee als o refuses to buy the Ministry’s 
explanation that lack of consensus among various Migrant organizations for permanent return and 
settlement is the main reason behind non-return of Migrants to the Valley. While there may be 
difference of opinion between the organizations, the perception in the community is that the situation 
on the ground is not at all conducive for return which is the main reason for the failure of the plan 
rather than lack of consensus among the organizations. The Committee is therefore of the opinion that 
some more components of the PM's package should be opened up for the Migrants without the 
conditionality of their return. This, in the view of the Committee, will serve as a confidence building 
measure encouraging the families to return to the Valley. 
(Para 2.1.11 of the 179th Report) 
Action Taken  
 
3.1.2 It is Government’s endeavour to provide various rehabilitation facilities to the Kashmiri 
migrants and to facilitate their return to the Valley. Various relief and rehabilitations packages are 
already being provided to Kashmiri Migrants. Government is providing cash relief, ration to eligible 
migrants and has constructed 5242 Two Room Tenements/ flats at four locations in Jammu and 200 
flats at Budgam in the Valley for the migrants with all basic amenities like schools, parks, health 
centers, community centers etc. A Package of ₹1618.40 crore was announced by the Prime Minister in 
2008 to facilitate the return of the migrants and their families to their homes. 469 transit 
accommodations have been constructed under the package and govt. jobs have been provided to 1553 
migrant youths and recruitment process of 1526 more govt. jobs is underway, which is likely to be 
completed soon.  
 
3.1.3 Moreover, in the Union Budget 2014-15, Rs.500 crore has been earmarked for rehabilitation of 
Kashmiri Migrants. A proposal has since been received from the Government of J&K for revision in 
the existing PM’s Package -2008. The proposal envisages upward revision of the scale of the most of
